triage.name: Cannabis
triage.reason: Substance use presentation with intoxication, withdrawal, and cannabis hyperemesis; reachable by history and tox screen, though framed as a use disorder rather than a single disease.

demographics: Most common illicit drug used in the US; use is more prevalent in adolescents and young adults
Use is reported more often by males than females
Higher rates of use in states with legal recreational cannabis
More common in people with other substance use, including alcohol and tobacco

risk_factors.text: Other substance use, including alcohol or tobacco
Family history of substance use disorder

family_history: Substance use disorder in a first-degree relative
social_history: Use before driving or at work or school
Trying to cut down or quit and having trouble doing so
Legal or school consequences related to use
exposures: Smoked joints, blunts, pipes, or bongs

chief_complaints.text: I smoke weed every day and I can't seem to stop
I've been throwing up over and over and nothing helps
I feel anxious and shaky when I don't use it
My parents made me come in because of my marijuana use
I've been feeling paranoid and spaced out since I used

hpi.onset: Often begins in the teens or early twenties, frequently with occasional social use that escalates over months to years
hpi.duration: Chronic, often years of use by the time of presentation
hpi.progression: Increasing frequency and amount over time, sometimes with a switch to stronger products such as concentrates or vape cartridges; may progress to daily use and difficulty cutting back
hpi.quality: Patients describe a relaxed, euphoric 'high' with altered time sense and increased appetite; with heavy use, they describe feeling foggy, unmotivated, or needing it just to feel normal
hpi.severity: Variable; some present for a routine visit, others after an emergency such as severe vomiting or a panic reaction
hpi.timing: Often daily or several times a day; withdrawal symptoms appear within a day or two of stopping and peak over the first week
relieving: For hyperemesis, hot showers or baths

associated_symptoms.text: Trouble sleeping, especially when cutting back
Feeling foggy or having trouble with memory and focus
Repeated episodes of nausea, vomiting, and belly pain in heavy long-term users
Panic, paranoia, or hallucinations after high doses

pertinent_negatives: Symptoms that began before any cannabis use

positives.text: Feeling hot or sweaty during withdrawal

negatives: Persistent psychosis between episodes of use

general.mild: Awake, alert, relaxed; may appear mildly euphoric or giggly; no distress
general.moderate: Sedated or mildly disinhibited; conjunctival injection; speech may be slow; cooperative
general.severe: Markedly sedated or agitated; disoriented to time or place; poor coordination; may be diaphoretic from repeated vomiting
general.critical: Obtunded or severely agitated with paranoid or hallucinatory behavior; unable to cooperate with exam; signs of dehydration or hemodynamic instability

findings.maneuver: Inspect the conjunctivae in room light
findings.finding: Red, injected conjunctivae without discharge or photophobia

findings.maneuver: Check pupillary size and reactivity to light
findings.finding: Pupils equal, round, and reactive; normal size
No exudate, no tonsillar swelling, no drooling

findings.maneuver: Auscultate the heart and palpate the radial pulse
findings.finding: Regular tachycardia without murmur or gallop
Normal S1 and S2 without murmur, rub, or gallop
Diffuse expiratory wheeze
Clear breath sounds without crackles or wheeze

findings.maneuver: Palpate the abdomen, starting away from any pain
findings.finding: Mild epigastric or periumbilical tenderness without guarding or rebound
Soft, non-tender, no organomegaly or mass
Warm, dry skin without rash or track marks
Cool, diaphoretic skin

findings.maneuver: Observe the patient walking and perform a finger-to-nose test
findings.finding: Unsteady gait or impaired coordination

findings.maneuver: Perform a focused neurologic exam including strength, sensation, and cranial nerves
findings.finding: No focal weakness, sensory loss, or cranial nerve deficit

findings.maneuver: Check for nystagmus on horizontal and vertical gaze
findings.finding: Horizontal nystagmus
Alert and oriented to person, place, and time; intact attention and recall
Disorientation, inattention, or impaired short-term recall

findings.maneuver: Observe behavior and ask about suspiciousness or hallucinations
findings.finding: Paranoid or suspicious behavior, or reported hallucinations
No focal deficit

labs.caveat: Dehydration and poor oral intake during cannabinoid hyperemesis can produce ketonuria; a positive result is nonspecific.
Low bicarbonate reflects vomiting and volume depletion in cannabinoid hyperemesis; a normal value does not exclude it.
Elevated from dehydration and poor intake during hyperemesis.
Hypokalemia from repeated vomiting; check before giving fluids.
Rises with dehydration from hyperemesis; a normal value does not exclude significant volume loss.
Hypoglycemia can occur with poor intake and vomiting; check before attributing altered mental status to cannabis alone.
Ordered to exclude thyroid disease when vomiting, anxiety, or tachycardia is prominent.
Negative. Required in anyone who could be pregnant before attributing nausea and vomiting to cannabis.
Ordered when epigastric pain is prominent to exclude pancreatitis.

findings.finding: Sinus tachycardia
Normal sinus rhythm at 60–100 bpm
Normal QT interval
Normal PR and QRS intervals without block
No ST elevation or depression
No T-wave inversion

findings.text: Usually normal; no dilated loops or free air

imaging.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast
imaging.preferred_when: Severe or atypical abdominal pain, or when another cause is suspected

findings.text: No bowel obstruction, perforation, or inflammatory mass
Gastric distension or air-fluid levels from vomiting

imaging.study: Ultrasound of the right upper quadrant
imaging.preferred_when: Epigastric or right upper quadrant pain to exclude biliary disease

findings.text: No gallstones or gallbladder wall thickening

initial.why: Rules out pregnancy before attributing nausea and vomiting to cannabis
Assesses dehydration, electrolyte losses, and renal function in vomiting or withdrawal
Looks for ketones, infection, or other causes of symptoms
Excludes hypoglycemia as a cause of altered mental status or weakness
Screens for infection or anemia when symptoms are atypical

confirmatory.why: Detects cannabis metabolites; supports recent use but does not establish a use disorder or hyperemesis

confirmatory.test: Clinical interview for cannabis use disorder
confirmatory.why: The diagnosis rests on history of impaired control, craving, and continued use despite harm; no laboratory test confirms it

supporting.why: Excludes thyroid disease when anxiety, tachycardia, or vomiting is prominent
Excludes pancreatitis when epigastric pain is prominent
Adds evidence for an inflammatory cause when infection is suspected
supporting.only_if: infection or inflammatory process is suspected

supporting.why: Screens for obstruction or perforation when vomiting is severe
supporting.only_if: severe or persistent vomiting with abdominal distension

not_indicated.test: ct abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast
not_indicated.why: Not routine; reserve for severe or atypical abdominal pain or suspected surgical cause
not_indicated.only_if: severe or atypical abdominal pain, or another cause is suspected

not_indicated.why: No role unless focal neurologic deficits or new seizures are present
No role in uncomplicated cannabis use or hyperemesis
Not indicated unless chest pain or ischemic symptoms are present
Not routine; order only if co-ingestion is suspected and clinically relevant

decision_points: Pregnancy test before attributing vomiting to cannabis in anyone who could be pregnant
Urine drug screen supports recent use but a negative result does not exclude cannabis use disorder
Consider cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome in heavy long-term users with recurrent vomiting and compulsive hot showers
Evaluate for alternative causes when focal neurologic deficits, fever, or severe abdominal pain are present

criteria.name: Cannabis use disorder (paraphrased)
criteria.summary: A problematic pattern of cannabis use leading to impairment or distress, with at least two of the following in a 12-month period: using more or longer than intended; persistent desire or unsuccessful efforts to cut down; spending a lot of time obtaining, using, or recovering; craving; failure to fulfill obligations at work, school, or home; continued use despite social or interpersonal problems; giving up important activities; using in physically hazardous situations; continued use despite physical or psychological problems; tolerance; withdrawal.
items: Using more or longer than intended
Persistent desire or unsuccessful efforts to cut down
Spending a lot of time obtaining, using, or recovering
Continued use despite social or interpersonal problems
Continued use despite physical or psychological problems

criteria.name: Cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome (clinical)
criteria.summary: A syndrome in heavy, long-term cannabis users characterized by recurrent episodes of severe nausea and vomiting, abdominal pain, and compulsive hot showers or baths that relieve symptoms; symptoms improve with cannabis cessation.
items: Compulsive hot showers or baths that relieve symptoms

differential.name: Cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome
differential.why_considered: Recurrent severe nausea and vomiting in a heavy long-term cannabis user

history: Compulsive hot showers or baths that relieve symptoms
Episodes recur in a similar pattern
exam: Mild epigastric tenderness without peritoneal signs
labs: Hypokalemia and low bicarbonate from vomiting
Elevated BUN and creatinine from volume loss
imaging: Abdominal imaging normal without obstruction or inflammation

differential.name: Cyclic vomiting syndrome
differential.why_considered: Stereotyped recurrent episodes of severe vomiting separated by symptom-free intervals

history: Episodes begin in childhood or young adulthood
Hot showers do not reliably relieve symptoms
Personal or family history of migraine
Acute onset over hours to a day
labs: Usually normal or mild electrolyte changes

differential.name: Acute pancreatitis
differential.why_considered: Severe epigastric pain with nausea and vomiting
differential.trigger: Severe epigastric pain radiating to the back, especially with alcohol use

history: Constant severe epigastric pain radiating to the back
labs: Lipase elevated more than three times the upper limit of normal
imaging: Pancreatic edema or peripancreatic fluid on CT

differential.name: Cannabis intoxication
differential.why_considered: Recent use with euphoria, sedation, and impaired coordination

history: Symptoms begin within minutes to hours of use
labs: Urine drug screen positive for cannabis metabolites

differential.name: Cannabis withdrawal
differential.why_considered: Irritability, anxiety, insomnia, and decreased appetite after stopping heavy use

history: Symptoms begin within a day or two of stopping
labs: Urine drug screen may be positive or negative depending on timing

differential.name: Alcohol intoxication or withdrawal
differential.why_considered: Altered mental status, vomiting, and autonomic symptoms in a patient who uses substances
differential.trigger: Tremor, sweating, and tachycardia after stopping alcohol, or ataxia and slurred speech with recent drinking

history: Symptoms begin hours to days after last drink
Prior withdrawal seizures or delirium tremens
exam: Ataxia, dysarthria, or confusion with intoxication
labs: Elevated AST and ALT with AST greater than ALT

differential.name: Serotonin syndrome
differential.why_considered: Agitation, tachycardia, diaphoresis, and altered mental status in a patient taking serotonergic drugs
differential.trigger: Recent addition or dose increase of a serotonergic medication with clonus or hyperreflexia

labs: Normal or mildly elevated creatine kinase

differential.name: Primary psychotic disorder
differential.why_considered: Paranoia or hallucinations in a young person who uses cannabis

history: Psychotic symptoms persist between episodes of use
Symptoms began before cannabis use or continue with abstinence
labs: Urine drug screen may be positive but does not explain persistent symptoms

differential.name: Major depressive disorder
differential.why_considered: Low mood, fatigue, and decreased appetite in a patient who uses cannabis

history: Depressed mood or anhedonia most of the day for at least two weeks
Sleep and appetite changes independent of use

severity.mild: Occasional use with mild euphoria, no functional impairment, and no withdrawal symptoms
severity.moderate: Regular use with cravings, tolerance, and mild withdrawal symptoms such as irritability and insomnia when stopping; some problems at school or work
severity.severe: Daily heavy use with impaired control, continued use despite harm, and prominent withdrawal; may include recurrent vomiting from cannabinoid hyperemesis or a panic reaction
severity.critical: Severe agitation with paranoia or hallucinations, or cannabinoid hyperemesis with dehydration, hypokalemia, and acute kidney injury requiring IV fluids

red_flags.finding: Severe agitation with paranoia or hallucinations
red_flags.meaning: Acute psychosis; needs close observation and may require antipsychotic treatment

red_flags.finding: Persistent vomiting with inability to keep fluids down
red_flags.meaning: Dehydration and electrolyte loss; needs IV fluids and electrolyte replacement
Volume depletion or another acute process; needs urgent evaluation

red_flags.finding: Focal weakness, numbness, or new seizure
red_flags.meaning: Not explained by cannabis; evaluate for a structural or vascular cause

red_flags.finding: Chest pain or syncope after use
red_flags.meaning: Possible cardiac complication; needs ECG and further workup
Immediate safety risk; needs psychiatric evaluation

complications.name: Cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome
clues: Compulsive hot showers that relieve symptoms

complications.name: Withdrawal syndrome
clues: Irritability, anxiety, insomnia, and decreased appetite within a day or two of stopping

special_populations.differences: Adolescent use can interfere with brain development and is associated with poorer school performance; presentation is often driven by a parent or school rather than the patient.
Less common but increasing; may present with falls, confusion, or interactions with other medications; use may be for medical symptoms such as pain or insomnia.
Use during pregnancy is associated with lower birth weight and problems with fetal and child development; screening and counseling are important, and abrupt cessation should be supported.
Smoked cannabis carries a risk of fungal and other respiratory infections; consider this in patients with neutropenia or transplant.
Cannabinoids are metabolized in the liver; effects may be prolonged and stronger in patients with cirrhosis.

key_questions.question: How often do you use cannabis, and how much on a typical day?
key_questions.looking_for: Daily or near-daily use; escalating amounts over time

key_questions.question: How long have you been using, and when did it become regular?
key_questions.looking_for: Years of use, often starting in the teens or early twenties

key_questions.question: How do you use it — smoked, vaped, edibles, dabs, concentrates?
key_questions.looking_for: High-THC products such as concentrates or vape cartridges raise risk of dependence and hyperemesis

key_questions.question: Have you tried to cut down or stop? What happened?
key_questions.looking_for: Failed attempts to cut down; a core feature of cannabis use disorder

key_questions.question: Do you get cravings, or feel irritable, anxious, or unable to sleep when you are not using?
key_questions.looking_for: Withdrawal symptoms beginning within a day or two of stopping and peaking in the first week

key_questions.question: Has your use caused problems at school, work, or home, or with relationships?
key_questions.looking_for: Failure to meet obligations, giving up activities, or continued use despite problems

key_questions.question: Have you ever used before driving or in other risky situations?
key_questions.looking_for: Use in physically hazardous situations; impaired driving

key_questions.question: Have you had repeated episodes of severe vomiting with belly pain? Do hot showers or baths help?
key_questions.looking_for: Cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome: recurrent vomiting with compulsive hot showers that relieve symptoms

key_questions.question: Do you use alcohol, tobacco, or other drugs?
key_questions.looking_for: Co-occurring substance use, which is common and affects treatment

key_questions.question: Have you felt depressed, anxious, or had thoughts of harming yourself?
key_questions.looking_for: Co-occurring depression, anxiety, or suicidal ideation

key_questions.question: Have you ever felt paranoid or heard or seen things that were not there, especially after using?
key_questions.looking_for: Cannabis-induced psychosis; symptoms that persist between episodes of use suggest a primary psychotic disorder

key_questions.question: Are you pregnant, or could you be pregnant?
key_questions.looking_for: Pregnancy status; use in pregnancy affects fetal development

key_questions.question: Does anyone in your family have a problem with alcohol or drugs?
key_questions.looking_for: Family history of substance use disorder

key_questions.question: Do you take any medications, including prescribed, over-the-counter, or herbal?
key_questions.looking_for: Interactions and other causes of symptoms

reasoning_points: A problematic pattern of cannabis use causing impairment or distress, with features such as using more than intended, failed attempts to cut down, craving, and continued use despite harm
Tolerance and withdrawal (irritability, insomnia, decreased appetite, anxiety) support the diagnosis
Urine drug screen supports recent use but does not confirm a use disorder; a negative result does not exclude it
Cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome should be considered in heavy long-term users with recurrent vomiting and compulsive hot showers
Pregnancy must be excluded before attributing vomiting to cannabis
Alternative causes such as pancreatitis, gastroenteritis, or primary psychotic disorder should be considered when symptoms are atypical

easy: Young adult with daily use and clear functional impairment
Conjunctival injection and relaxed affect on exam
medium: Patient presents with vomiting and abdominal pain, requiring recognition of cannabinoid hyperemesis
Co-occurring anxiety or depression that complicates the picture
Adolescent brought in by a parent, with limited self-report
hard: Older adult with falls and confusion, where cannabis use is not initially disclosed
Pregnant patient with nausea and vomiting, requiring careful distinction from hyperemesis gravidarum
Patient with paranoia that persists between episodes of use, raising concern for a primary psychotic disorder
